**1. Observation schedule – 40 observations/month across three shifts** | Shift | Approximate number of nurses (out of 32) | Proportion of total observations | Observations per month | |-------|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------|------------------------| | Day | 12 – 13 | ~37 % | **15** | | Evening | 10 – 11 | ~31 % | **13** | | Night | 9 – 10 | ~32 % | **12** | *Why this split?* The unit’s staffing pattern is roughly 38 % day, 31 % evening and 31 % night. By mirroring that distribution the audit workload reflects real‑world exposure to hand‑hygiene opportunities. ### Auditor rotation | Month | Auditor A | Auditor B | |-------|-----------|-----------| | Day | 8 | 7 | | Evening | 6 | 7 | | Night | 5 | 7 | *Both auditors together perform the full 40 observations. If a shift has an odd number of observations, one auditor takes the extra one.* **Observation cadence** - **Day shift (8 am–4 pm)** – 15 observations spread evenly: 3 per hour from 9 am to 3 pm. - **Evening shift (4 pm–12 am)** – 13 observations: 2 per hour from 5 pm to 11 pm, plus one at 4 pm and one at midnight. - **Night shift (12 am–8 am)** – 12 observations: 1 every two hours starting at 12 am. Auditors should avoid predictable patterns; they will use a random‑time generator or a pre‑printed “observation window” list to keep the audit covert and representative. --- **2. What each auditor must record for a valid observation** | Item | Description | Why it matters | |------|-------------|----------------| | **Date & time** | Exact timestamp of the hand‑hygiene opportunity (HHO). | Enables trend analysis, shift comparison, and audit integrity checks. | | **Shift & ward location** | Day/Evening/Night + specific bay or procedure area. | Identifies high‑risk zones and staffing patterns. | | **Nurse identifier** | Anonymous code (e.g., N01–N32). | Allows compliance tracking by individual without breaching confidentiality. | | **Patient ID** | Anonymous patient number or “P‑” code. | Confirms that the HHO is patient‑related, per WHO definition. | | **WHO ‘Five Moments’ category** | 1 = Before touching a patient; 2 = Before clean/aseptic procedure; 3 = After body fluid exposure risk; 4 = After touching a patient; 5 = After touching patient surroundings. | Core audit metric – compliance is measured against the correct moment. | | **Hand‑hygiene action taken?** | Yes / No (and if no, reason: e.g., “not required”, “forgot”). | Primary outcome variable. | | **Product used** | Alcohol‑based rub, soap & water, or none. | Helps identify product‑specific gaps and supply issues. | | **Technique compliance** | 0 = Not performed; 1 = Performed but technique incomplete (e.g., missed palm); 2 = Fully compliant. | Adds depth to the audit beyond binary compliance. | | **Duration of hand hygiene** | Seconds (if recorded). | Useful for process improvement and training focus. | | **Barriers observed** | Physical (no dispenser), time pressure, glove use, etc. | Provides actionable insights for interventions. | | **Observer initials & signature** | Auditor A or B + digital signature if possible. | Ensures accountability and audit trail. | *All data are entered into the unit’s electronic audit sheet (or a secure spreadsheet) immediately after each observation to minimise recall bias.* --- **3. Presenting monthly results to the unit** | Format | Content | Visuals | |--------|---------|---------| | **Executive summary (1‑page)** | • Overall compliance rate
• Highest‑ and lowest‑performing shifts
• Key barriers identified | • One‑line bar chart of overall vs. shift rates | | **Detailed report (2–3 pages)** | • Total HHO count, compliant moments, non‑compliant moments
• Compliance by WHO moment (1–5)
• Product usage distribution
• Technique compliance breakdown
• Individual nurse trend (anonymized) | • Stacked bar chart: compliance per shift
• Heat map: compliance by moment
• Line graph: monthly trend over past 6 months | | **Action‑plan slide** | • Targeted interventions (e.g., dispenser placement, refresher training)
• Responsible person & deadline | • Gantt‑style timeline for next month’s actions | ### How to deliver 1. **Unit huddle (15 min)** – Present the executive summary and key findings. 2. **Nurse‑lead briefing (30 min)** – Dive into the detailed report, discuss barriers, and solicit feedback on feasibility of interventions. 3. **Documentation** – Upload the full report to the unit’s shared drive; pin a concise version in the break room and on the unit intranet. ### KPI dashboard (optional) - **Compliance %** (overall & per shift) – target ≥ 90 % by Q4 2026. - **Moment‑specific compliance** – track improvement for moments 3 & 5, which are often lowest. - **Barrier resolution rate** – percentage of identified barriers addressed within one month. --- ### Quick reference: Observation schedule template | Shift | Auditor | Observation times (HH:MM) | |-------|---------|---------------------------| | Day | A | 09:00, 10:30, 12:00, 13:30, 15:00 | | Day | B | 09:45, 11:15, 12:45, 14:15, 15:45 | | Evening | A | 17:00, 18:30, 20:00, 21:30, 23:00 | | Evening | B | 17:45, 19:15, 20:45, 22:15, 23:45 | | Night | A | 00:00, 02:00, 04:00, 06:00, 08:00 | | Night | B | 01:00, 03:00, 05:00, 07:00 | *Adjust times slightly each month to avoid pattern recognition.* --- **Bottom line:** By allocating the 40 observations in proportion to staffing levels, recording a comprehensive set of data points for every hand‑hygiene opportunity, and presenting results in clear, actionable formats, the unit will have a robust audit cycle that drives measurable improvement across all shifts.
